title: Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease Hold Rate Relief for a Clean Returned-Payment Record
content:
**Q&A for lease-end representatives — returned payments and the hold rate, Kestrel Closed-End Consumer Lease**

**The rule.** The hold rate returned-payment relief is 5 percentage points (the clean returned-payment relief) when no payment on the lease was ever returned, 2 percentage points (the single returned-payment relief) when exactly one payment on the lease was returned, and nothing when two or more were. The relief is subtracted from the hold rate before the rate is applied.

*What counts as a returned payment?* A payment on the lease that was dishonoured and reversed. Every such reversal over the life of the lease counts, whatever the bank's reason.

*Does a payment that was returned and then made good again stop counting?* No. The count is of payments that were returned.

| Payments on the lease ever returned | Relief |
|---|---|
| 0 | 5 points |
| 1 | 2 points |
| 2 | nothing |
| 3 or more | nothing |

**Hypothetical illustration**: a hold rate of 25 percent on a lease that never had a payment returned becomes 20 percent before it is applied; with one returned payment it becomes 23 percent.
